text:
amanda: Quick q about the embeddings endpoint: does truncation happen per-item or per-batch? I'm ingesting variable-length docs with an upstream chunker and need deterministic indexes for the vectors.

raj: truncation is per-input by default, not per-batch. we apply the model's token limit to each item individually, then embed. why—running into issues? :thinking:

amanda: yeah one doc got cut mid-sentence and now the downstream index vs source mapping is off. if we chunk we want a one-to-one mapping: input chunk -> vector. just want to confirm we can't hit a case where a batch-level truncation would drop the tail of the last item.

lee: correct — we truncate each input to model_max_tokens before encoding. batching only affects throughput, not per-input token decisions. we also return the original input length and truncated_length in metadata for hosted API users.

maria: small caveat: if you pass an empty string we return a zero-length vector? currently we return a deterministic vector (all zeros) and a warning field. is that causing trouble?

amanda: that was the other thing — sometimes the chunker produces empty strings (split on "") and the client lib filters them inconsistently. what does the official contract say about empty inputs and vector shape?

raj: contract: for N inputs -> response.vectors is an array of length N. each vector is a float array of dimension D (model-specific). empty input -> return vector of length D filled with 0.0 and a per-item warning code `EMPTY_INPUT` in the response.errors array. no items are dropped or re-ordered.

amanda: perfect. what about pad_to param? I saw docs mention `pad_to` for aligning all vectors in a batch — is that server-side padding or client indicator?

lee: `pad_to` is a request-level hint that pads/truncates inputs to a token count before embedding so you can control consistency across items. it's optional. if set, truncation happens after pad_to is applied (i.e., pad then truncate to model limit). default is null (no pad).

maria: NOTE: pad_to increases compute cost because padding expands tokenization length. use with caution if you care about cost.

amanda: good to know. one more: batching split behavior — if I send 1500 small items and server batch_size is 512, do we get vectors in the same order as inputs across batches?

raj: yes order is preserved. we chunk into internal batches but we guarantee stable ordering in the output. mapping is index-based. we also include `input_index` in each vector entry for sanity.

amanda: nice. could we get a small example of the exact response shape for 3 inputs (one normal, one empty, one long-truncated)?

lee: sure — example response shape:```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v1",
  "vectors": [
    {"input_index": 0, "vector": [0.123, -0.045, ...], "orig_length": 85, "truncated_length": 85},
    {"input_index": 1, "vector": [0.0, 0.0, ...], "orig_length": 0, "truncated_length": 0, "warning": "EMPTY_INPUT"},
    {"input_index": 2, "vector": [0.342, -0.11, ...], "orig_length": 12000, "truncated_length": 2048, "warning": "TRUNCATED"}
  ],
  "model_dim": 1024
}
```

maria: fwiw API will return a 400 with code `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` if a single input's tokenized length exceeds our hard cap for the model even before pad_to is considered (we try to avoid this by stating model limits clearly).

amanda: good. if we change truncation defaults in the future (breaking?), what's our backwards-compatibility plan? we need to ensure downstream index/ordering doesn't change.

raj: plan: never change ordering behavior. we may change default pad/truncate numeric thresholds but will add a response field `truncation_policy_version` and a Deprecation header for >=30 days when defaults change. clients can explicitly opt-in to a new policy via a request flag to opt out of surprises.

lee: ops note: adding an automated alert in console when a project sees >1% `TRUNCATED` warnings across requests in last 24h. opsbot will post incidents/alerts in #eng-oncall.

amanda: thanks everyone — this clarifies. I'll add tests in the chunker integration to filter empty strings and assert vector length and ordering. tagging @maria for API docs update. :thumbsup:

maria: on it, will add a small RFC section about `pad_to`, `EMPTY_INPUT`, and `truncation_policy_version` to the /docs/api/embeddings page.

opsbot: Deploy note: embeddings-hosted v1.3 will include `truncation_policy_version` metadata; rollout scheduled 2027-06-15 03:00 UTC.
